review_highlights.comment: Honestly the class is not that bad if you do the readings like she asks you to do. You will see that the slides aren't as important if you read the textbook. Professor Irvine was the worst! I usually give all my professors a try and she mentally drained me within the first week of being in her class I had to drop it. She spends less then 60 seconds on a slide and wont even share presentations with you. She wouldnt even let you take a drink of water. She goes over time and gets upset if you pack Up.

Dr. Irvine is amazing. Her classes can be challenging, but if you put in the work it is worth it. She tries to get to know all of her students- even if her classes consist of over 50 students. She did not sugar coat any history, and I learned so much from her class. Decent amoutn of work, but so worth it.

Professor Irvine & her course is mentally draining. Lots of reading and FAST note taking. Talks for full 75 minute class and then some every single time. Requires students to complete a make up assignment if they miss class, which is an extremely ridiculous paper. Does not require textbook, but highly encourages it to understand different concepts.

Prof Irvine is probably the only professor at IU who actually cares about her students and wants them to succeed. There are weekly readings/document analysis worksheets & weekly quizzes, none of which are too hard. She will give you the midterm/final before hand - both are all open-ended. Pay attention in class, take good notes and you'll be fine.

review_highlights.comment: An amazing instructor!   Iram Tariq will teach you things about her home culture that you couldn't imagine ever happening here in the US. Like most instructors her lectures can be disconnected from what is on the tests, but the stories and information she brings to the table is  above-all-else. Iram is very cultured and knowledgable. What she discusses in class sometimes is off track, but the information you get from her is so unique and rare because of her life experiences. Do the reading from the assigned pages in the book and you will be fine. Iram is hilarious and one of my favorite teachers I've had at IU so far.

I loved Iram! She has been one of my favorite professors at IU. She has a lot of interesting stories, she's hilarious, and has great lectures. Most importantly, she cares about her students more than anything. She's always willing to help. Urban Problems was an easy course as long as you showed up to class, took notes, and studied for exams.

Iram is very intimidating but i promise you get used to her and end up liking her. she will put you on the spot so pay attention. just do what she says, and youll be fine. exams are very easy, straight from powerpoint slides. shes very caring about if you understand the lecture and tries to help a lot. shes scary but she makes you learn.

Great class, great professor. Iram is such a funny and interesting Professor, she makes the class interesting. As long as you show up and pay attention you should be good. The tests in the class follow her powerpoints exactly, so pay attention to those. I would highly recommend this course and professor.

analysis.name: Carl Ipsen
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 56 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment:
Do you prefer saving your sanity?

Coming from a (now ex-)straight A student for seven semesters, Dr. Ipsen is knowledgeable on the course material, but his grading is harsh. He's paranoid about ChatGPT usage, yet grades harshly if papers don't read as if they're ChatGPT-written.

I spent more time on his class than CHEM 383: Human Biochemistry.

Very interesting class- Carl is very passionate and knowledgable about sicilian mafia and the class expectations are really straightforward. 2 Blue book exams the whole semester and 8 writing assignments- if you do them all the course is pretty easy to get an A in. Also offers extra credit clicker questions that are straight from that day's lecture

B226 was a very engaging course despite being online. Dr. Ipsen assigned a very reasonable amount of work every week. My one complaint is that he is overly suspicious about the possibility of students using ChatGPT, but this did lead to our midterm and final getting canceled. TA's grade most of the writing assignments, not Dr. Ipsen.

readings each week, you have to make a discussion question and reply to 2 each class. not that bad considering theres not any other work outside of class. small quiz in class for attendance over reading material. if you go to class and at least have a general understanding of readings, youll get an A. I'd take his classes again for sure

The Mafia class is hard, but extremely interesting. Professor Ipsen is very knowledgeabl, but intimidating. His assistants grade very hard. There are 9 very short written assignments (only have to write roughly 2 paragraphs) and two exams. However, there is a lot of material and people covered so you must be ready to memorize and STUDY! Not easy.

analysis.name: Christoph Irmscher
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: If you have the chance to take a class with him, do it! He is probably the best professor I have had at IU.  Very intelligent, yet funny and down to earth.  We got to visit the Lily Library, Art Museum, and Opera.  He helped me finally understand poetry and was more than willing to help me with my papers.  My writing definitely improved

If you have the chance to take a class with him, do it. There aren't many reviews, so trust me on that. As others have said, he genuinely cares about his student, both as academics and as people. He is a bank of knowledge, yet funny and down-to-earth. Caring and approachable and helpful. He truly represents the best parts of academia.

Dr. Irmscher is a great professor.  He is one of the most down-to-earth academics I think you'll meet.  He makes himself available even though he's very busy.  Although he's native German, the man speaks English better than me.  The class is engaging; attendance is highly encouraged.  Take a class with him! You won't regret it.

The class is engaging, and he shows a real passion for his topic. Though he is often busy, he makes himself very available for his students and is willing to help with papers and such. He has reading for each class period, but it isn't excessive. There were several enjoyable visits to the Lilly Library to see original copies.

Christoph is an exceptional professor. An advocate for his students, he desires to see students succeed and schedules individual conferences to help papers become the best they can be. I've taken 3 classes with him. I would recommend him to anyone.

If you attend class, you will get an A. He is super knowledgeable on research/grad school, so if that's the goal, Dr. Katona will be great. If not, its still a fun class.

Istvan is easily one of my favorite professors. He's an expert in his field, passionate about teaching, and genuinely cares about students. I'm disabled, so can struggle with attendance, but he never made me feel bad. Instead, he asked how he could support me. He loves getting questions and made me feel extremely welcomed in classes. A++ professor.

I took two classes with Dr. Katona - "Intro. to Molec. and Cell. Mech. of Addiction" and "Adv. in Molec. and Cell. Mech. of Addiction". 

While material was dense at times, he always ensured that everyone understood the material. Very patient and kind. Grew and learned a lot in his class. 

Put the work in and ask good questions, you'll get an A!

Dr. Katona is very interesting and insightful, but he clearly has favorites. If you are not one of the people he deems important, he will not care about what you have to say. Overall, a decently easy course, but I would not recommend to someone else in the future. You would be better off to take another class with another professor.
This is to offset my bad review from earlier. Seriously, if you need an upper level neuro class, it is a great one to take. Lower commitment than most others I have taken!

Prof Isaac goes above and beyond for his students: sharing optional interesting articles, adapting the syllabus to follow current events, and arranging for relevant guest speakers. Very thoughtful, very caring. Facilitates discussions exceptionally and makes sure every student has room to speak.

Always willing to listen and provide feedback.

I took Y-212 with him and his class is fine overall and pretty easy, but my god, is he annoying. As someone else said, his god complex is crazy. He gets mad at students for not participating when he asks the most inane questions. If you can avoid him do it.

review_highlights.comment: Isra is easily one of the best Spanish teachers Ive ever had. Grammar is a dull subject but he manages to keep class fun and interesting. He cares about his students and does everything he can to make sure they succeed and understand the material. Hes passionate about motivating students to pursue a major or minor, and successful at it too!

Israel is a professor who really wants you to succeed. He makes himself available outside of class. He also gives a lot of extra credit opportunities to increase participation grades. His feedback is always positive, and he keeps class interesting.

Israel is an amazing prof! He encourages students and gives great feedback, he brings the class together in "familias", he has a strong passion for helping students succeed and makes himself available. Israel inspired me to turn my Spanish minor to a major after I considered dropping it altogether. If you're struggling or want a fun prof, take him!

Very encouraging and overall great person. He provides many extra credit opportunities, if you do anything somewhat related to Spanish outside of class he'll give you points for it. He cares a lot about his students and their success. He even offered to write me letters of recommendation for scholarships to study abroad. Favorite professor so far!

Israel is a very good spanish teacher. The class is not difficult, but requires you to study, just as any spanish class would. The tests are departmental, so every test will be similar no matter what professor you have. Israel is hilarious and calls the class "la familia". He does his best to make class fun. I recommend him.

analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I would say that he not only understood the materials, he made sure we understood the materials. With showing different student examples in class and the way of breaking down the mathematics, it became clear to a lot of students. Without his aide, this class would be more difficult. He is an instructor who genuinely cares about our learning.

I liked how this instructor was very understanding, personable, and thorough with his lessons. He also had our best interest at mind with learning the material and asked plenty of times if we needed help. He was also very available to answer questions and went above and beyond to reach out if we were struggling.

He worked very hard and taught the course well. I liked how the course put us students in the shoes of our future students, and the instructor emphasized the fact that our future students won't have the understanding we do, so we need to think like them. He was always willing to help students no matter how long it took until they fully understood.

He was very welcoming and had high energy while teaching. He made our learning a very big part of the course and you can see how much he wanted us to improve. The course was structured by doing a lot of examples and practice problems which were helpful too. However, it was sometimes hard to understand the material (math is not my strong suit).

I liked the way this course made me think about math in a unique way. I liked how my instructor was very easy to talk to. He also was very responsive and open to being able to help me with the course. He responded to emails very fast and very flexible in terms of asking questions about assignments.

review_highlights.comment: Iulia has an accent, but if you go to class and pay attention it is not hard to understand. She provides so many practice tests that it is really all on you if you receive a bad grade in this class. Watch the Finite Show.

She is a little difficult to understand but as long as you aren't sitting next to a freshman boy who just cant get over talking about how much he loves his new frat, then you should be okay. She puts notes online so all you have to do is print them off, take them to class and follow along. Its not that hard. I love this class. Shes a great teacher.

Finite is a difficult course but Iulia is not more difficult than other professors. Sometimes she teaches the hard stuff before the easier stuff which makes it a little hard to follow but if you do the problems in the book before class it makes it easier to understand. Her accent is different, but she's very accessible outside class and cares.

She has a very strong accent, kids are going to complain about finite but if you just go to class, take good notes, and do the homework the tests aren't hard. An A in this class is certainly not easy, but it is very possible. She's a very nice lady and knows the content well, you just have to pay attention.

She is the hardest teacher to understand in this school. She is not only unclear about how to do class work and homework but half of the time she is confused herself and doesn''t know how to do the problems. Absolutely awful explanation skills and only confuses people more.  Doesn''t speak English well.

His lectures and long and a bit boring, but its clear that he wants his students to succeed. I am not good at econ so went to office hours often, which are one on one which really helped me understand the content. 3 exams make up most of the grade, but there are clear study guides provided, also a lot of extra credit opportunities.

I would rather walk for an hour in freezing weather, barefoot, on concrete, than take class with this professor. Does FRQ on exams, which NO other teacher does. Also has very few assignments/extra credit, so tests are your grade. This course felt like an exercise rather than education, and it hindered my ability to learn the material.

Ivan is def a nice person but be prepared to get a tutor. His lectures are not aimed at teaching the material because he expects you already understand it. The exams have FRQs which other econ classes do not have so take this as your warning

The class is manageable, I wouldn't worry about his rating score. Yes, he has an accent but he's a decent teacher and as long as you show up and do the work, chances are you'll do fine. + the extra credit you receive is a nice bonus. I would definitely recommend you take this class with her.
